subject: anatomy
title: Synovial Joint Types and Cartilage Varieties

steps.tx: Synovial joints exhibit diverse geometric contours determining their permitted movement axes. An **ellipsoid joint**, or condyloid articulation, pairs an oval convex condyle with an elliptical concavity. Operating as a biaxial articulation, it enables flexion, extension, abduction, and adduction along perpendicular planes, while bony geometry prevents active axial rotation.
steps.say: Synovial joints exhibit distinct shapes that dictate their permitted axes of motion. An ellipsoid joint pairs an oval convex surface with an elliptical concavity. Functioning as a biaxial joint, it allows flexion, extension, abduction, and adduction while restricting axial rotation.

vis.alt: Articular surfaces and synovial membrane lining
vis.caption: Synovial joint architecture showing articular cartilage and capsule. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The radiocarpal wrist joint and the metacarpophalangeal joints of the fingers represent premier examples of an ellipsoid joint. In contrast, a uniaxial articulation permitting pure rotation around a single longitudinal pivot pin is classified as a **pivot joint**, or trochoid articulation. A central bony peg rotates within a ring formed by bone and a retaining fibro-osseous ligament.
steps.say: The wrist joint and knuckle metacarpophalangeal joints exemplify ellipsoid articulations. Conversely, a uniaxial joint allowing pure rotation around a single axis is a pivot joint. A bony peg spins within an osseoligamentous ring.

steps.tx: Classic pivot joints include the median atlantoaxial joint, where the dens of the axis rotates inside the atlas held by the transverse ligament, and the superior radioulnar joint. When maximal multi-axial freedom is required, a **ball and socket joint** pairs a spherical head with a cup-shaped socket, permitting movement across three orthogonal axes including circumduction and axial rotation.
steps.say: Classic pivot joints encompass the median atlantoaxial joint and the proximal radioulnar joint. When multi-axial motion is needed, a ball and socket joint seats a globular head into a cup-like socket, permitting angular movement in any plane plus rotation.

steps.tx: Skeletal elements and joints rely upon three specialized varieties of cartilage distinguished by their extracellular matrix. The most abundant type is **hyaline cartilage**, characterized by a glass-like homogeneous matrix enriched with type II collagen fibrils. It blankets articular surfaces, builds the costal cartilages, and constitutes the temporary cartilaginous skeleton of the human embryo.
steps.say: The human skeleton incorporates three cartilage varieties defined by their matrix composition. The most widespread is hyaline cartilage, marked by a glassy matrix packed with type two collagen fibrils. It coats articular surfaces and builds costal cartilages.

vis.alt: Histological features of hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage
vis.caption: Cartilage types: hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage microarchitecture. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Articular hyaline cartilage lacks an overlying perichondrium, meaning it cannot regenerate through chondroprogenitor recruitment following mechanical erosion. Where flexibility and resilient elastic recoil are demanded, the tissue incorporates dense networks of elastin fibres, forming **elastic cartilage**. This pliant cartilage shapes the auricle of the ear, the external acoustic meatus, the epiglottis, and the cuneiform cartilages.
steps.say: Articular hyaline cartilage lacks a perichondrium and therefore exhibits poor intrinsic reparative capacity. When flexible recoil is required, dense elastin networks create elastic cartilage. This pliable tissue supports the external ear, epiglottis, and auditory tube.

right.title: Elastic Cartilage
points: Elastin meshwork plus type II collagen

steps.tx: Subjected to tremendous tensile and compressive stresses, **fibrocartilage** combines the durability of dense fibrous tissue with the elasticity of cartilage. Packed with alternating rows of chondrocytes and coarse bundles of type I collagen, it lacks a true perichondrium. Fibrocartilage constructs intervertebral discs, the pubic symphysis, the glenoid and acetabular labra, and intra-articular menisci.
steps.say: Designed for tremendous tensile strain, fibrocartilage blends dense collagen fibres with cartilaginous elasticity. Packed with type one collagen bundles and chondrocytes, it lacks a perichondrium. It forms intervertebral discs, pubic symphyses, and knee menisci.

steps.tx: Joint innervation governs proprioception, pain perception, and protective muscular reflexes. According to the anatomical principle of **Hilton law**, the nerve supplying a joint also innervates the muscles moving that joint and the skin over their dynamic insertions. This coordinated neural wiring ensures that joint injury automatically triggers protective muscle spasm to splint the damaged articulation.
steps.say: Joint innervation governs position sense and pain feedback. Under Hilton law, a nerve that supplies a joint also supplies the muscles that cross it and the skin over their insertions. This shared wiring induces protective muscle guarding after joint injury.

steps.tx: A classic application of Hilton law occurs at the knee joint, which receives sensory innervation from the femoral, obturator, and tibial nerves. Because the **obturator nerve** supplies both the hip joint and the knee, inflammatory disease of the hip often presents deceptively as referred pain localized entirely to the medial aspect of the knee.
steps.say: A classic example of Hilton law involves the knee joint, supplied by femoral, obturator, and tibial branches. Because the obturator nerve innervates both the hip and knee, children with hip pathology often complain solely of referred medial knee pain.
